_doc: Inflation benchmarks for retrospective editions dated in 2024: the target for the current calendar year as publicly known at each cutoff. End-2023 state of the verified 2023 register (its 2023 changes applied: China's ~3% of 5 Mar 2023, New Zealand's remits of 27 Jun and 13 Dec 2023, Australia's Statement of 8 Dec 2023; general note carried unchanged), updated for the 2024 current-year targets set earlier: Brazil 3.25 -> 3.0% +/-1.5 (CMN Res. 4,918 of 24 Jun 2021, art. 1, 'para o ano de 2024 ... 3,0%'; DOU 25 Jun 2021; no normativos PDF exists for it, so the BCB's exibenormativo record and Agencia Brasil's same-day report are cited); Indonesia 3.0 -> 2.5% +/-1 (PMK 101/PMK.010/2021, Art. 2(3)(c)); Thailand 2.0, the midpoint of the 1-3% range approved by the Cabinet on 26 Dec 2023 for 2024 (THE STANDARD and the Bangkok Post the same day; BoT MPC announcement No. 2/2566 of 26 Dec 2023, its English translation cited from its file's creation on 27 Dec 2023); Turkiye 5%, 'the inflation target set jointly with the Government', +/-2pp, to be reached 'in the medium-term' (CBRT Monetary Policy for 2024, 29 Dec 2023, para 2; the current PDFs were re-saved on 26 Dec 2024, so the text is corroborated by Bloomberg HT's report of 29 Dec 2023); Colombia 3% (Board of 30 Nov 2023, 'reitera la meta de inflacion del 3% como guia y objetivo de su politica'; its +/-1pp is a forecast band, not a target range; read from the site's print rendering, date confirmed by Valora Analitik the same day). Korea's 2% is carried (the BoK's 2024 operation direction of 28/29 Dec 2023 restates it). Change announced during 2024: China's Report on the Work of the Government delivered 5 Mar 2024 (CPI 'around 3%', value unchanged; recorded as the new year's objective; applies from 2024-03-10). Value-unchanged reaffirmations are not recorded: the FOMC's of January 2024; the BoJ's statement of 19 Mar 2024 ending the negative interest rate policy and YCC ('With the price stability target of 2 percent'); the UK remit letter of 14 Nov 2024; the BoK's two-yearly review of 18 Dec 2024. Targets set during 2024 for later years are not recorded (Brazil's Decree 12,079 / CMN Res. 5,141 of 26 Jun 2024, a continuous 3% target from 2025; Indonesia's PMK 31/2024 for 2025-2027; Poland's guidelines of 3 Sep 2024; Thailand's Cabinet of 24 Dec 2024; the CBRT's text for 2025 of 25 Dec 2024; Colombia's Board of 29 Nov 2024), nor is anything announced after the last edition's cutoff of 28 Dec 2024. No new Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy (Australia) or monetary policy remit (New Zealand; the Gazette notice of 10 Dec 2024 is the Financial Policy Remit) was issued in 2024; the ECB, Fed, Bank of Canada, SNB, Riksbank, Norges Bank, RBI, Banxico, SARB, NBP, MNB, CNB and Banco Central de Chile targets are unchanged (for CH, SE, NO, IN, MX, PL, CZ, CL, ZA and CA this rests on searches, as in the 2023 register).
note: Where an official objective refers to an index other than headline CPI (the Federal Reserve's PCE price index; see each row), the benchmark is applied to headline CPI. India's benchmark is the RBI's stated CPI objective for the current period. Benchmarks apply to the headline CPI series used here. Each benchmark is the target for the current calendar year as publicly known at the cutoff; China's is the government's annual CPI objective from its Report on the Work of the Government (until that report, the previous year's applies). Where a range was set, its midpoint is used; for the euro area, the ECB's symmetric 2% target. Sources are listed only if published on or before the edition’s last eligible day.

US.wording: FOMC Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy as amended 27 Aug 2020: the longer-run goal of 2 percent PCE inflation is kept, and the Committee 'seeks to achieve inflation that averages 2 percent over time', so that 'following periods when inflation has been running persistently below 2 percent, appropriate monetary policy will likely aim to achieve inflation moderately above 2 percent for some time' (value unchanged).
US.index: PCE price index; benchmark applied to headline CPI

urls.label: Federal Reserve press release, 'Federal Open Market Committee announces approval of updates to its Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy', 27 Aug 2020

XM.wording: ECB strategy review, 8 Jul 2021: 'The Governing Council considers that price stability is best maintained by aiming for a 2% inflation target over the medium term. This target is symmetric, meaning negative and positive deviations of inflation from the target are equally undesirable' (replacing 'below, but close to, 2%'; HICP remains the measure).

urls.label: ECB press release, 'ECB's Governing Council approves its new monetary policy strategy', 8 Jul 2021

JP.wording: 'The "Price Stability Target" under the Framework for the Conduct of Monetary Policy', 22 Jan 2013: 'the Bank sets the "price stability target" at 2 percent in terms of the year-on-year rate of change in the consumer price index (CPI)' (replacing the 1% 'price stability goal' of February 2012); in the joint statement with the Government the Bank will 'aim to achieve this target at the earliest possible time'.

urls.label: Bank of Japan, The "Price Stability Target" under the Framework for the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 22 Jan 2013
Joint Statement of the Government and the Bank of Japan on Overcoming Deflation and Achieving Sustainable Economic Growth, 22 Jan 2013

GB.wording: June Budget 2010: 'the independent Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Bank of England will continue to target 2 per cent inflation, as measured by the 12-month increase in the Consumer Prices Index (CPI)'.

urls.label: HM Treasury, Budget 2010 (June, HC 61), 22 Jun 2010, para 1.27

CA.wording: Joint Statement of the Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada on the Renewal of the Monetary Policy Framework, 13 Dec 2021: 'The target will continue to be defined in terms of the 12-month rate of change in the total CPI. The inflation target will continue to be the 2 percent mid-point of the 1 to 3 percent inflation-control range'; the agreement runs for another five-year period, beginning with 2022. 'The primary objective of monetary policy is to maintain low, stable inflation over time'; monetary policy 'should continue to support maximum sustainable employment', and the Bank 'will continue to use the flexibility of the 1 to 3 percent control range to actively seek the maximum sustainable level of employment when conditions warrant' (value unchanged).

urls.label: Bank of Canada, Joint Statement of the Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada on the Renewal of the Monetary Policy Framework, 13 Dec 2021

AU.wording: Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy agreed by the Treasurer and the Reserve Bank Board, 8 Dec 2023 (responding to the Review of the Reserve Bank): 'The Reserve Bank Board and the Government agree that a flexible inflation target is the appropriate framework for achieving price stability, recognising the importance of low and stable inflation. They agree that an appropriate goal is consumer price inflation between 2 and 3 per cent'; 'The Reserve Bank Board sets monetary policy such that inflation is expected to return to the midpoint of the target' (midpoint 2.5%, value unchanged; recorded because the Statement is replaced: the 2016 Statement's 'on average, over time' gives way to an explicit midpoint).

urls.label: RBA, Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 8 Dec 2023
Treasurer, media release 'Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy', 8 Dec 2023

CH.wording: The SNB 'regards prices as stable when the national consumer price index (CPI) rises by less than 2% per annum' (midpoint of 0–2%: 1.0%).

urls.label: SNB Quarterly Bulletin 4/2007, 'Inflation forecasting as part of the monetary policy concept'

SE.wording: Riksbank, 7 Sep 2017: 'The Executive Board of the Riksbank has decided to adopt inflation measured in terms of the CPIF (the consumer price index with a fixed interest rate) as a formal target variable for monetary policy. The target for monetary policy is that the annual change in the CPIF shall be 2 per cent, that is, the same level previously applied to the CPI'; a variation band of 1–3 per cent replaces the ±1pp tolerance band, applying from the monetary policy decision of 6 Sep 2017.
SE.index: CPIF (CPI with a fixed interest rate); benchmark applied to headline CPI

urls.label: Sveriges Riksbank press release No. 21, 'CPIF target variable for monetary policy', 7 Sep 2017

NO.wording: Regulation on Monetary Policy laid down by the Government on 2 Mar 2018 (in force immediately; the 2001 regulation repealed from the same date), Section 3: 'The operational target of monetary policy shall be annual consumer price inflation of close to 2 percent over time. Inflation targeting shall be forward-looking and flexible so that it can contribute to high and stable output and employment and to counteracting the build-up of financial imbalances.' Norges Bank: 'The inflation target is now 2%, compared with the previous 2.5%.'

urls.label: Norges Bank Monetary Policy Report 1/18, 15 Mar 2018 (reproduces the Regulation of 2 March 2018 on Monetary Policy, p. 13)
Norges Bank, Executive Board's assessment, Monetary Policy Report 1/18, 15 Mar 2018

NZ.wording: Amended Remit for the Monetary Policy Committee issued by the Minister of Finance with the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Economic Objective) Amendment Bill, passed on 13 Dec 2023, which returns the Reserve Bank to a single focus on price stability: 'The amended Remit retains an inflation target of 1% to 3% over the medium-term, with a focus on the 2% mid-point, and removes the objective to support maximum sustainable employment' (Reserve Bank of New Zealand, 13 Dec 2023; value unchanged; recorded because the remit is replaced).

IN.wording: On 31 Mar 2021 the Government retained the CPI inflation target at 4 per cent with lower and upper tolerance levels of 2 and 6 per cent for the next five years, from April 2021 (value unchanged; recorded because the statutory target was re-notified); the MPC's resolutions keep setting policy 'in consonance with the objective of achieving the medium-term target for consumer price index (CPI) inflation of 4 per cent within a band of +/- 2 per cent'.

(um e meio ponto percentual) e de mais 1,50 p.p. (um e meio ponto percentual)' (3.0% with a ±1.5pp tolerance band).

TR.wording: CPI inflation target of 5%, set jointly with the Government: the CBRT's Monetary Policy for 2024 (29 Dec 2023; the renamed successor of the 2023 'Monetary Policy and Liraization Strategy'), para 2: 'Enflasyon hedeflemesi rejimi çerçevesinde, Hükümet ile birlikte belirlenen enflasyon hedefi yüzde 5 olarak korunmuştur. TCMB’nin hesap verme yükümlülüğünün bir unsuru olan belirsizlik aralığı, önceki yıllarda olduğu gibi hedef etrafında her iki yönde 2 yüzde puan olarak korunmuştur. Para politikası enflasyonu orta vadede bu hedefe ulaştıracak şekilde oluşturulacaktır.' ('Under the inflation targeting regime, the inflation target of 5% set jointly with the Government, has been maintained. The uncertainty band, which is an element of the CBRT’s accountability, has also been maintained at 2 percentage points in both directions around the inflation target, the same as the previous years. The monetary policy will be formulated to bring inflation to this target in the medium-term.'); para 3: 'The forecasts announced via Inflation Reports will serve as interim targets with a function to set a reference for inflation expectations.' The agreed 5% target is used; the Inflation Report interim targets are not.

KR.wording: Price stability target from 2019 set by the Monetary Policy Board on 26 Dec 2018, in consultation with the Government: 2% in terms of the year-on-year rate of change in the consumer price index ('2019년 이후 물가안정목표'를 소비자물가 상승률(전년 동기 대비) 기준 2.0%로 확정 의결), the same level as the 2016–2018 target; the three-year application period is abolished (no fixed period), with the operation of the target reviewed every two years ('3년마다 재설정했던 물가안정목표의 적용기간을 없앴다. 다만, 2년 주기로 물가안정목표 운영 개선에 필요한 사항을 점검키로 했다').

CL.wording: Updated framework document 'La Política Monetaria del Banco Central de Chile en el Marco de Metas de Inflación' (published 11 Feb 2020): 'El nivel de meta para la inflación está fijado en 3% anual. Ello significa que la política monetaria se orienta a que la variación anual del IPC fluctúe en torno a 3%' and 'El propósito práctico u objetivo operacional de la política monetaria es que la inflación proyectada se ubique en 3% anual en un horizonte de política en torno a dos años' (value unchanged; the ±1pp range no longer defines the target: inflation 'debería fluctuar la mayor parte del tiempo en un rango de entre 2 y 4%').

urls.label: Diario Financiero, 'Banco Central actualiza marco de la política monetaria' (in Spanish), 12 Feb 2020

CO.wording: Board of Directors, 30 Nov 2023: 'La Junta Directiva del Banco de la República reitera la meta de inflación del 3%'; 'La JDBR reitera la meta de inflación del 3% como guía y objetivo de su política' ('The Board reiterates the 3% inflation target as the guide and objective of its policy'); 'Las acciones de política monetaria, que han contribuido a reducir la inflación, están encaminadas a llevar a la inflación a la meta y velan porque la actividad económica transite por una senda sostenible en el tiempo.' The release restates no target range: its 'más o menos 1 punto porcentual' is a forecast band ('Se prevé que la inflación se ubique alrededor del 3%, en un rango de más o menos 1 punto porcentual, en un horizonte entre 12 y 18 meses'). The Banco de la República's page sits behind a bot check; its text was read from the site's print rendering and its date is confirmed by the page itself and a same-day report quoting it.

urls.label: Banco de la República, 'La Junta Directiva del Banco de la República reitera la meta de inflación del 3%' (in Spanish), 30 Nov 2023
Valora Analitik, 'Junta del BanRep ve inflación cerca del 3% en 12-18 meses: confirma meta de 3% en largo plazo' (in Spanish), 30 Nov 2023

TH.wording: Monetary-policy target for 2024 approved by the Cabinet on 26 Dec 2023, as agreed between the Minister of Finance and the Monetary Policy Committee: headline inflation within the range of 1–3 percent as the medium-term price-stability target and the target for 2024 ('กำหนดให้อัตราเงินเฟ้อทั่วไปในช่วง 1-3% เป็นเป้าหมายของนโยบายการเงินด้านเสถียรภาพราคาสำหรับระยะปานกลาง และเป็นเป้าหมายของนโยบายการเงินสำหรับปี 2567', THE STANDARD; Bangkok Post: 'The cabinet on Tuesday approved the Bank of Thailand's (BoT) headline inflation target range of 1% to 3% for 2024, unchanged from this year'; BoT Notification No. MPG. 2/2566, unofficial translation, para 3.2: 'The Minister of Finance and the MPC mutually agreed to set the monetary policy target for price stability such that headline inflation would reside within the 1.0 – 3.0 percent target range for the medium-term horizon and for the year 2024'); a range with no point target, the same as for 2023 (midpoint 2.0% used).
